encounters.cc: Recurrent fevers and skin infections since early infancy with poor wound healing

lines: Recurrent fevers and skin infections since early infancy with poor wound healing

The patient is an infant with established X-linked chronic granulomatous disease and medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency who returns for ongoing management of recurrent infectious complications.
They recall that his umbilical cord stump took nearly a month to separate after birth.
Minor scrapes on his knees and elbows take unusually long to heal and rarely produce any visible pus despite redness and swelling.
He has had multiple episodes of gingival swelling and skin infections that have required antibiotic therapy but have been slow to resolve.
